title: Standard refund window is 30 days from purchase
body: Customers on monthly self-serve plans can request a full refund within 30 days of the original charge. After day 30, direct them to cancel instead of refunding — no exceptions without manager sign-off.

title: Enterprise annual contracts are non-refundable
body: Once an enterprise annual contract is signed and the first invoice is paid, it is non-refundable for the remainder of the term. Customers can still downgrade or cancel auto-renewal for the following year.

title: Downgrades issue a prorated partial refund
body: When a customer downgrades mid-cycle from a higher-tier plan, credit the prorated difference back to their account balance rather than the original payment method, unless they explicitly ask for cash back.

title: Chargebacks escalate straight to finance
body: Any chargeback notification from the payment processor must be forwarded to finance within one business day, before support responds to the customer directly. Do not issue a competing refund while a chargeback is open.

title: Goodwill credits are capped without manager approval
body: Support can issue a goodwill credit of up to $50 per customer per quarter without approval. Anything above that requires a support manager's sign-off logged in the ticket.

title: Commit messages follow conventional commit format
body: Every commit subject line starts with a type prefix (feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor) followed by a colon and a short imperative summary. Body text explains why the change was made, not just what changed.

title: Pull requests need two approvals before merging to main
body: No pull request merges to the main branch with fewer than two approving reviews from other engineers. A single approval is enough for feature branches that don't deploy directly.

title: Never force push to a shared branch
body: Force pushing to main, staging, or any branch other engineers have already pulled is prohibited — it silently discards their commits. Force push is only allowed on a branch you own exclusively.

title: Never commit secrets or .env files to the repository
body: API keys, database passwords, and signing secrets must never be committed, even in a private repo. Use the deploy platform's secret manager and keep .env gitignored; a leaked key gets rotated immediately, not just deleted from history.

title: New features roll out behind a percentage-based feature flag
body: Ship risky changes behind a feature flag starting at 5% of traffic, doubling every 24 hours if error rates stay flat, before going to 100%. Skip the ramp only for a hotfix to an already-broken feature.

title: SEV1 incidents page the on-call engineer immediately
body: Any incident classified SEV1 (full outage or data loss risk) must page the on-call engineer within 5 minutes of detection, day or night. Do not wait for a human to confirm the severity first — the alert itself pages.

title: Legal threats from a customer escalate to legal same day
body: If a customer mentions a lawsuit, subpoena, or regulator in a support conversation, stop responding substantively and loop in the legal team the same business day. Never admit fault or promise a specific remedy before legal weighs in.

title: Churn-risk signals from enterprise accounts notify the CSM
body: If an enterprise account shows two or more churn-risk signals (usage drop, failed renewal call, executive sponsor departure) in a rolling 30 days, notify the assigned customer success manager the same day.

title: Security incidents notify the CISO within one hour
body: Any confirmed security incident — unauthorized access, data exposure, or credential compromise — must reach the CISO within one hour of confirmation, before any public communication goes out.

title: Repeated refund requests from one customer get flagged to fraud
body: A customer requesting more than three refunds in a rolling 90 days gets flagged to the fraud review queue automatically, even if each individual request looked legitimate on its own.

title: Multi-factor authentication is required for all admin accounts
body: Every account with admin-level access to production systems or customer data must have MFA enabled before it's granted access. An admin account without MFA gets suspended automatically after a 7-day grace period.

title: Offboarded employees have access revoked within 24 hours
body: When an employee's last day is confirmed, IT must revoke all system access — SSO, VPN, shared drives, admin panels — within 24 hours. Manager notification of departure triggers the ticket automatically.

title: New vendors touching customer data require a security review
body: Before signing any contract with a vendor that will process or store customer data, security must complete a vendor risk review and sign off. This applies even to short pilot engagements.

title: Customer data exports require manager approval
body: Any bulk export of customer data — for debugging, analytics, or a customer request — needs a support or engineering manager's approval logged before the export runs, regardless of how the data will be used.

title: API keys rotate every 90 days
body: Every service-to-service API key and customer-issued API key rotates on a 90-day schedule by default. Customers get a 14-day warning email before their key expires so integrations don't break unexpectedly.

title: First response to a support ticket is due within 4 business hours
body: Every new support ticket gets a substantive first response — not an auto-reply — within 4 business hours of being opened, regardless of plan tier. Tickets opened outside business hours count from the next business day's start.

title: Enterprise-tier tickets get a 1-hour response SLA
body: Tickets from accounts on the enterprise plan carry a 1-hour first-response SLA instead of the standard 4-hour one, and route directly to the dedicated enterprise support queue rather than the general pool.

title: Weekend support coverage handles critical issues only
body: Weekend on-call support only triages tickets tagged critical (service down, data loss, security). Non-critical weekend tickets sit until Monday morning rather than paging the weekend on-call engineer.

title: Non-English tickets route to a language specialist
body: A ticket detected in a language other than English routes to the on-shift language specialist for that language instead of the general queue. If no specialist is on shift, hold the ticket rather than reply machine-translated.

title: Resolved tickets can be reopened within 7 days
body: A customer replying to a resolved ticket within 7 days reopens the original ticket instead of creating a new one, preserving history for the agent. After 7 days, any reply starts a fresh ticket.

title: Receipts are required for expenses over $25
body: Any individual expense line over $25 needs an attached receipt in the expense report; anything at or under that threshold can be submitted without one. This applies to every expense category, not just travel.

title: International travel requires pre-approval
body: Book international travel for work only after getting written pre-approval from your manager, including destination and estimated cost. Domestic travel under the standard budget doesn't need pre-approval.

title: Meal per diem is capped by city cost tier
body: Meal reimbursement while traveling follows a per diem cap set by the destination city's cost tier (tier 1 cities like New York or London get a higher cap than tier 3 cities). Actual receipts aren't required under the per diem model.

title: Client entertainment expenses need director-level approval
body: Meals, event tickets, or other entertainment spent on a client require approval from a director or above before reimbursement, regardless of the amount. Log the client and business purpose in the expense note.

title: Personal vehicle mileage is reimbursed at the IRS standard rate
body: Using a personal vehicle for work travel is reimbursed per mile at the current IRS standard mileage rate, updated whenever the IRS publishes a new one. Commuting to your regular office doesn't count.

title: Vendors handling customer data must be SOC 2 Type II certified
body: Before any vendor contract is signed, the vendor must provide a current SOC 2 Type II report covering the systems that will touch customer data. A SOC 2 Type I report or a self-attestation is not sufficient — the audit must cover a full observation period, not just a point-in-time design review.

title: EU-headquartered vendors may substitute ISO 27001 for SOC 2
body: Vendors headquartered in the EU can satisfy the vendor security certification requirement with a current ISO 27001 certificate instead of SOC 2 Type II, since ISO 27001 is the standard EU auditors and regulators recognize. US-headquartered vendors still need SOC 2 Type II; ISO 27001 alone doesn't substitute for them.

title: GDPR data subject access requests are fulfilled within 30 days
body: When an EU customer requests a copy of, correction to, or deletion of their personal data under GDPR Article 15, respond within 30 calendar days of the verified request. Extensions of up to 60 additional days are allowed only for genuinely complex requests, documented in writing to the requester.

title: CCPA data subject requests are fulfilled within 45 days
body: California residents requesting access to or deletion of their personal data under the CCPA get a response within 45 calendar days of the verified request, with one 45-day extension allowed if we notify the requester before the first deadline. This window is longer than GDPR's — do not apply the GDPR timeline to a CCPA request or vice versa.

title: Data breach notifications to regulators go out within 72 hours
body: Once a data breach involving personal data is confirmed, notify the relevant data protection regulator within 72 hours per GDPR Article 33. This is a separate, external-facing obligation from internal CISO notification — the CISO must already know before this clock starts, but the regulator notification has its own deadline and its own written record.

title: Handling protected health information requires a signed BAA
body: Any vendor or subprocessor that will touch protected health information (PHI) must sign a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) under HIPAA before integration begins. This is in addition to, not instead of, the standard vendor security review — a signed BAA without a completed security review does not clear a vendor to go live.

title: Personally identifiable information is encrypted at rest
body: Any personally identifiable information (PII) stored in a production database is encrypted at rest using AES-256, with keys rotated on the same 90-day schedule as API keys. This applies to backups and replicas, not just the primary database.

title: Closed support ticket data is retained for 90 days after resolution
body: Ticket content, attachments, and transcripts for a resolved support ticket are retained for 90 days after closure, then permanently deleted unless the ticket is linked to an open legal hold or an active refund/chargeback dispute. This retention window applies regardless of the customer's plan tier.

title: Vendor security certifications are reassessed annually
body: Every vendor's SOC 2 Type II report or ISO 27001 certificate is re-collected and reviewed annually, not just at initial signing — a certification that lapses without a renewed report on file triggers a review of whether the vendor relationship continues. This applies to every vendor under the security review process, regardless of which certification they originally qualified under.

title: EU customer data is stored in EU-region infrastructure
body: Production data for customers billed under an EU entity is stored and processed in EU-region infrastructure only — no cross-region replication to US or APAC data centers, including backups. This is a data residency requirement, separate from the GDPR request-response timelines that govern what happens once data is stored.

title: Third-party penetration tests run annually
body: An external penetration test of production systems runs at least once every 12 months, performed by a vendor independent of our infrastructure and security teams. Findings rated high or critical get a remediation deadline of 30 days; the test itself is separate from vendor certification requirements.

title: SEV2 incidents notify the on-call engineer within 30 minutes
body: A SEV2 incident (partial outage or significant degraded performance, no full outage) sends a non-paging Slack notification to the on-call engineer within 30 minutes of detection, rather than the immediate page a SEV1 triggers. The on-call engineer still has to acknowledge it, just without waking anyone up outside business hours.

title: SEV3 incidents are logged but don't notify anyone
body: A SEV3 incident (minor, no customer-visible impact) is logged in the incident tracker for trend analysis but doesn't page or notify the on-call engineer at all. It gets reviewed in the next weekly reliability sync instead.

title: VIP-designated accounts get a 15-minute first-response SLA
body: Accounts explicitly flagged VIP by sales (not just any enterprise-tier account) get a 15-minute first-response SLA, faster than the standard enterprise 1-hour SLA. The VIP flag is set manually per account and reviewed quarterly — enterprise tier alone doesn't qualify.

title: Free trial cancellations within 14 days get a full refund
body: A customer who converts directly from a free trial to a paid plan can cancel and receive a full refund within 14 days of the first charge, separate from and shorter than the standard 30-day refund window that applies to customers who weren't on a trial. After 14 days, the standard 30-day-from-purchase policy no longer applies either — the trial refund window is final.

title: CI status checks must pass before a pull request can merge
body: Every pull request needs a green build, passing tests, and a passing lint job before it's mergeable to main — GitHub branch protection enforces this, it's not optional or reviewer-discretionary. A reviewer cannot approve around a red CI check.

title: Changes deploy to staging before production
body: Every deploy goes to staging first and needs a smoke test pass there before promoting to production, no exceptions for small changes. Hotfixes for an active incident are the only case that can skip the staging gate, and only with a second engineer's sign-off in the incident channel.
